title: add transactional downgrade guards, backup/restore verification, and version pinning for private installer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Private deployments require deterministic upgrade and rollback behavior for on-prem and VPC customers. This PR adds three complementary pieces: (1) transactional downgrade guards that prevent accidental schema downgrades and enforce version pinning for operator-managed components, (2) a backup/restore verification step to the installer to validate automated backups before destructive migrations, and (3) explicit version-pinning metadata and tooling hooks for Helm and Terraform modules so rollbacks can be executed safely. Motivation: customers have hit edge cases during rapid rollouts where partial migrations left clusters in an unrecoverable state. These changes are designed to make upgrades and emergency rollbacks safer and auditable for Private installations. What I changed: - Add a transactional migration guard implemented as a lightweight coordinator that runs pre- and post-migration verification steps and writes a single 'upgrade_transaction' record to the installer state store. The coordinator can abort migrations if validation fails and exposes a recovery path to replay/rollback migrations. - Add explicit version pinning to Helm charts (Chart.yaml + values) and Terraform module inputs with schema validation and warning messages when unspecified. - Add backup/restore verification step: the installer now takes a temporary restore snapshot into a staging namespace and runs smoke checks (DB schema version, service liveness, basic API health) before proceeding with destructive operations. - Add SQL migration wrappers to ensure migrations are applied transactionally where supported and provide a rollback script for each migration that updates the installer state. - Add CLI flags and config options: --force-downgrade to allow admins to override downgrade guard (requires linear ticket/approval token), --backup-verify-timeout, and --migration-safety-check-level. - Docs: installer upgrade and rollback runbook, troubleshooting steps, and a sample Linear workflow for approval tokens. - Tests: unit tests for the coordinator, integration test that simulates failed migration and verifies automatic rollback path, and an e2e smoke that runs backup-restore-verify. Checklist: - [x] add coordinator and transactional guard implementation - [x] add helm chart version pinning and warnings - [x] add terraform module input validation for pinned versions - [x] implement backup/restore verification flow - [x] add CLI flags and config validations - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] update docs and runbook - [x] run internal canary upgrade on staging Summary of risks and mitigations: - Risk: false-positive guard aborts legitimate upgrades. Mitigation: configurable safety-check-level and clear admin override with audit token. - Risk: backup verification increases upgrade time. Mitigation: configurable timeout and option to parallelize verification for large datasets. Testing and rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag 'upgrade_transactional_guards'. - Canary rollouts to 2 staging clusters (internal) -> 3 beta customers. - Collect logs/metrics via observability hooks added in this PR. Related work and references: Linear: ENG-9121 (upgrade rollback tooling), ENG-9145 (private-installer migrations), ENG-9199 (backup/restore verifier). Jira: SUP-4481 (customer incident triggered request).
